theory.intro: Three results let you move between a single surd and a product or quotient of surds. They hold for $x>0$ and $y>0$. Each works both ways, so you can join surds or split them apart.
facts: Check the form first — a square, a product of two roots, or a quotient of two roots — then pick the matching result.
The results say nothing about addition or subtraction — only about squares, products and quotients.

workedExamples.solution_text:
Since $13>0$, taking the square root undoes squaring.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\sqrt{13^2}\\&=13\end{aligned}$

Multiply the radicands inside one square root.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\sqrt{6}\times\sqrt{7}\\&=\sqrt{6\times7}\\&=\sqrt{42}\end{aligned}$

workedExamples.question_text: Write $\dfrac{\sqrt{28}}{\sqrt{7}}$ as a single square root, then evaluate.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Divide the radicands inside one square root.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\dfrac{\sqrt{28}}{\sqrt{7}}\\&=\sqrt{\dfrac{28}{7}}\\&=\sqrt{4}\\&=2\end{aligned}$

workedExamples.question_text: Write $\sqrt{\dfrac{7}{10}}$ as a quotient of two surds.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Apply the square root to both the numerator and denominator.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\sqrt{\dfrac{7}{10}}\\&=\dfrac{\sqrt{7}}{\sqrt{10}}\end{aligned}$

workedExamples.question_text: Write down the values of $\sqrt{49}$, $\sqrt{100}$ and $\sqrt{4900}$. Hence show that $\sqrt{49}\times\sqrt{100}=\sqrt{4900}$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
$\sqrt{49}=7$, $\sqrt{100}=10$ and $\sqrt{4900}=70$.
Substitute these values into the product.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\sqrt{49}\times\sqrt{100}\\&=7\times10\\&=70\\&=\sqrt{4900}\end{aligned}$

workedExamples.question_text: Write down the values of $\sqrt{3600}$, $\sqrt{25}$ and $\sqrt{144}$. Hence show that $\sqrt{3600}\div\sqrt{25}=\sqrt{144}$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
$\sqrt{3600}=60$, $\sqrt{25}=5$ and $\sqrt{144}=12$.
Substitute these values into the quotient.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\sqrt{3600}\div\sqrt{25}\\&=60\div5\\&=12\\&=\sqrt{144}\end{aligned}$

foundation.question_text: Use $\sqrt{x}\times\sqrt{y}=\sqrt{xy}$ to write $\sqrt{3}\times\sqrt{5}$ as a single surd.
Use $\sqrt{x}\times\sqrt{y}=\sqrt{xy}$ to write $\sqrt{2}\times\sqrt{15}$ as a single surd.
Use $\dfrac{\sqrt{x}}{\sqrt{y}}=\sqrt{\dfrac{x}{y}}$ to write $\sqrt{10}\div\sqrt{5}$ as a single surd.
Use $\dfrac{\sqrt{x}}{\sqrt{y}}=\sqrt{\dfrac{x}{y}}$ to write $\dfrac{\sqrt{30}}{\sqrt{3}}$ as a single surd.
Use $\sqrt{x}\times\sqrt{y}=\sqrt{xy}$ to write $\sqrt{2}\times\sqrt{7}$ as a single surd.

development.question_text: Use $\sqrt{\dfrac{x}{y}}=\dfrac{\sqrt{x}}{\sqrt{y}}$ to write $\sqrt{\dfrac{3}{5}}$ as a quotient of two surds.
Use $\sqrt{\dfrac{x}{y}}=\dfrac{\sqrt{x}}{\sqrt{y}}$ to write $\sqrt{\dfrac{2}{15}}$ as a quotient of two surds.
Use $\sqrt{x}\times\sqrt{y}=\sqrt{xy}$ to write $\sqrt{14}\times\sqrt{15}$ as a single surd.
Use $\sqrt{x}\times\sqrt{y}=\sqrt{xy}$ to write $\sqrt{21}\times\sqrt{10}$ as a single surd.
Use $\dfrac{\sqrt{x}}{\sqrt{y}}=\sqrt{\dfrac{x}{y}}$ to write $\dfrac{\sqrt{7}}{\sqrt{35}}$ as a single surd.
Use $\sqrt{\dfrac{x}{y}}=\dfrac{\sqrt{x}}{\sqrt{y}}$ to write $\sqrt{\dfrac{11}{6}}$ as a quotient of two surds.

mastery.question_text: Write down the values of $\sqrt{36}$, $\sqrt{225}$ and $\sqrt{8100}$. Hence show that $\sqrt{36}\times\sqrt{225}=\sqrt{8100}$.
Write down the values of $\sqrt{14400}$, $\sqrt{64}$ and $\sqrt{225}$. Hence show that $\sqrt{14400}\div\sqrt{64}=\sqrt{225}$.
Write down the values of $\sqrt{121}$, $\sqrt{256}$ and $\sqrt{30976}$. Hence show that $\sqrt{121}\times\sqrt{256}=\sqrt{30976}$.
